good.text: My bedroom has a bed, a door and zero armor stands. After {past_fort}, that is luxury.
They smoothed my walls. Took three years and a queue of twelve thousand jobs, but they did it.
My room is thirty levels above the Safety burrow. I sleep like a baby who reads the paper.
I have a cabinet now. I keep nothing in it. I just like opening it.
The Overseer gave me a room next to the still. For that, I forgive every throne.
My new bed is so soft I forgot to complain for a whole night.
My bedroom engraving shows a dwarf drinking. Simple. Hopeful. Rare in this world.
I can hear the mist ring from my pillow. It sounds like dampness and joy.
A bed, a chest and a door that shuts. I am basically a baron.
My room backs onto the catacombs. Quiet neighbours. Very respectful.
I got the room the last {prof} had. It still smells faintly of ambition.
Nobody has stored anything in my bedroom all week. I checked under the bed twice.
The bedroom door locks. I lock it. I unlock it. I lock it again. Freedom.
My room is so far from the trees that not a single branch can reach me.

bad.text: Woke up to seven armor stands in my room. The Overseer says they are 'in transit'.
My bed was moved into the Safety burrow 'for convenience'. Thirty levels down. By the stairs.
My room is rough stone. It is on the smoothing list at position fourteen thousand and something.
There is a throne in my bedroom. I did not ask for it. Nobody sits on it. It watches me.
My bedroom shares a wall with the garbage pit. The wall is losing.
The engraving in my room shows Quakefocus starving. Lovely thing to wake up to.
I was given a bedroom with no bed. The carpenter is making doors. Again.
Somebody dug a hallway through my room. I now sleep in a corridor with opinions.
A ghost from {past_fort} sits at the end of my bed asking if there is meat yet.
My bed is made from the tree that took a miner. I do not sleep well.
The mist ring sprays straight under my door. My pillow is a pond.
My room is so small I have to step outside to change my mind.
The last owner of my room died of thirst. There was a full mug on the shelf.
They put my bed in the execution tower. 'Temporary', says the Overseer. Everything is.

heads_good.text: ROOM HAS NO TREE IN IT

good.text: The Overseer ordered exactly one armor stand. I made one. The order stopped. I wept.
Smoothed a whole wall today. The queue went from 12,000 to 11,999. Progress!
I made a throne and nobody ordered another hundred. Historic.
The mayor filed no production violations against me this week. I may frame the silence.
Finished my job and nobody stood in the way. A {prof} can dream, and today I did.
I hid one rough gem from the jeweler. Some future mood will thank me.
My workshop has a stockpile, a door and a mug within reach. Peak fortress planning.
I threw refuse INTO the pit today and nobody asked me to haul it back out. Bliss.
I cut a gem so fine the liaison would ask for it at double the price.
I made a barrel and it went straight to the brewer. The thirst paradox weakens.
Built a windmill today. It turns, the mist sprays, everyone cheers up a little. Me too.
I am getting good at this. Not Quakefocus-armor-stand good, but good.
Today's work order was sensible and achievable. I checked it twice for traps.
I engraved a wall showing a dwarf drinking beside a full barrel. Instant classic.

bad.text: I made 400 armor stands this year. We have nine soldier slots. One is filled.
Twelve thousand smoothing jobs and three smoothers. I smooth in my dreams now.
The mayor charged me with a production order violation. Nobody told me the order.
Sent to gather plants across the whole map. In the rain. Then the rain gathered me.
Spent all day hauling garbage out of the pit while someone threw more in behind me.
I cut every rough gem in the fort. Now three moods want rough gems. I am the villain.
I am a carpenter. I was asked for barrels. I was made to make doors.
My workshop was built on the far edge of the map. I commute more than the caravan.
I have made so many thrones my hands are throne-shaped now.
My job was suspended because a tree was in the way. The tree won.
I was given a work order with a number I cannot pronounce. It is mostly zeros.
The Overseer moved my workshop but kept my job. I am now working in a field.
I am the only {prof} in {fort}. So all the {prof} work in {fort} is mine.
I made a masterwork and it went straight into a bin of armor stand parts.

good.text: Nothing to do all day and nobody died. In this world, that is a festival.
I spent an afternoon watching the windmills turn. They never ask for rough gems.
I reread the old papers from {past_fort}. Good times, in hindsight. Mostly hindsight.
Sat in the mist ring for an hour. Damp, happy, unbothered.
Idle! Me! No smoothing, no hauling, no thrones. I did not know what to do with my hands.
Counted every drink in the stockpile for fun. All there. Nobody thirsty. Delicious maths.
A slow day in {fort}. I named some of the armor stands. Gerald is my favourite.
Played 'spot the elf' at the depot. Found none. Won.
So little to do, I volunteered for the militia. They said the captain is plenty.
Watched a merchant wander about for an hour. He looked at a door. Riveting.
Nothing happened in the tavern today. I toasted the nothing. Twice.
Spent the afternoon guessing who the mayor will charge next. I was right twice.
I am pleasantly bored. Last time I was this bored, {past_fort} still had dwarves in it.
I sat on one of the thrones. Just to see. It was fine. A fine, quiet day.

bad.text: So bored I joined the militia. It is me and the captain, being off duty together.
Nothing to do but count the loose stones. Eight hundred. Counted twice. Still 800.
I stared at the empty sheriff's office for an hour. Nobody came. Nobody ever comes.
I asked for work and was told to wait. I have been waiting since the last Great Rewind.
So bored I read the mayor's violation reports. Most of them are about me, apparently.
No job, no idle area, no friends. I leaned on an armor stand. It leaned back.
Nothing to do in {fort}. Even the forgotten beasts seem to have other plans.
I wanted to sit on a throne. The Overseer says they are 'stock'. All of them.
Bored enough to visit the Safety burrow. I did not go. Barely.
Watched the garbage pit all afternoon. Things went in. Things came back out. Why.
Bored, and the tavern is full of armor stands again. Nowhere to even sit and sulk.
All my labors were switched off. I am now a decorative dwarf.
Went for a wander and ended up on a tree branch. Came down fast. I read the papers.
Even the liaison has more to do than me, and he only ever says there is much to share.

good.text: Met a migrant who also remembers {past_fort}. We swapped stories over plump helmets.
Had a chat with the militia captain. First conversation either of us had all season.
Made a friend in the tavern. We bonded over hating the smoothing queue.
A cat adopted me. I did not ask. I am not complaining.
A cousin wrote from a fort our kin reclaimed. They say hello, and also 'send ale'.
The liaison told me there is much to share. I chose to believe he meant with me.
I joined the windmill club. Membership: me and one mechanic. We are inseparable.
Had dinner with three dwarves and none of them mentioned the Safety burrow. Bonded.
Found someone else who likes the mist ring. We sit there and drip together.
All the {prof}s of {fort} had a get-together. There were two of us. Lovely.
Somebody remembered my name today. Twice. I am tearing up a bit.
I sat beside a stranger at dinner. Now we argue about thrones every meal. A friendship!
A child told me all about her strange mood. Plant cloth. I listened. We are friends now.
I bought the captain a mug. The militia now has a fan club. It is me.

bad.text: All my friends were sent down to the Safety burrow. Fifteen did not come back up.
No real conversation since {past_fort}. I talk to the loose stones. All 800 of them.
The militia captain is the loneliest dwarf here, and I am second. We have never spoken.
My only friend was a fisherdwarf whose mood wanted rough gems. I cannot talk about it.
Nobody in {fort} knows my name. The mayor does, but only for paperwork.
I tried to make friends at the depot. The elves talked about trees. I left.
I miss the old {past_fort} crew. Most of them are ghosts now, or worse, nobles.
I waved at someone across the hall. It was an armor stand. There are many. I wave a lot.
I sat with the liaison. He said there is much to share. Then he shared nothing.
Nobody sat with me at dinner. Not even the ghost.
My best friend moved into the tree district. You know how that goes.
I joined the militia to meet people. Nine empty places. Poor conversationalists.
I am lonely in a fort of over a hundred dwarves. That takes real talent.
I talk to the windmill. It turns away from me, which feels personal.

good.text: Finally got to make something I wanted, not something the Overseer counted.
I had a drink. In a mug. In a tavern. Every need I have just sighed with relief.
I needed to see something new. I saw the garbage pit empty. Truly new.
Needed a good argument. Found one: is the Safety burrow safe? I won. It is not.
Spent time with family and nobody had to be fetched down out of a tree.
I needed nature. I looked at a tree from a respectful distance. Fulfilling.
I needed to pray and the temple was not a stockpile today. Spirit topped up.
I needed a fight. A crate looked at me funny. I won.
I needed to learn something. Learned you can die of thirst beside 1,994 drinks. Wisdom!
I needed to be extravagant. I wore two socks of different metals.
I needed to help someone, so I found a moody weaver some plant cloth. Crisis averted.
Needed a party. The fort threw one. It was for the windmill. Still counts.
Needed to craft. Made a mug. Gave it to myself. Very satisfying loop.
All my needs are met. I suspect a trick, but I will enjoy it first.

bad.text: I need to make art. The Overseer needs armor stands. Guess who wins.
I need a drink and I am standing next to a barrel of it. I cannot explain this either.
I need to pray, and the temple is now holding three hundred thrones.
I need to be in nature. The last dwarf who got close to nature died on a branch.
I need excitement. All we have is smoothing. Twelve thousand jobs of it.
I need to fight. The captain says it is an 'Off duty' season. Every season is.
I need my family. They stayed at {past_fort}. Mostly as ghosts.
I need my friends. All of them are in the Safety burrow 'just in case'.
I need to do something creative. My last idea was cut into a gem and sold.
I need to wander. I wandered into a tree. Now I need first aid as well.
I need to learn. The library has no books, only bins of loose stones.
I need an argument. Nobody will argue with me because they are all smoothing.
I need something fancy. I asked for a gem. Every gem has been cut. Story of the fort.
I need to help. I helped haul trash out of the pit. Then I was told to haul it back.

good.text: My fever broke. This hospital actually had a doctor. Half the old ones did not.
The beast dust wore off. I can feel my beard again. It feels great.
I am not dizzy anymore. The room has stopped spinning. The windmills have not, thankfully.
Got better with no chief medical dwarf at all. Medicine is mostly confidence.
The swelling went down and my helmet fits again. The militia may yet claim me.
I was sick from the garbage pit, but I am better. I forgive the garbage. Not the pit.
Whatever the forgotten beast breathed on me has faded. I only glow a little now.
My cough is gone. I celebrated by breathing loudly in the dining hall.
Feeling healthy! I have taken this as permission to drink twice.
A week in the hospital: beds, buckets and soap. {past_fort} could never.
I was numb for days. Now I can feel my toes. They are cold. Hooray.
The doctor set my arm and nobody had to be found in a tree. Good week.
I am cured. The {prof}s of {fort} are thrilled, mostly because I owe them a mug.
My blisters healed. I have named the scars after the old forts.

bad.text: I am sick and the hospital has no doctor. Just like {past_fort}. Tradition.
The forgotten beast came up the stairs and coughed on me. I am now a color.
Caught something nasty hauling trash out of the pit. Then I was told to haul more.
My arm is swollen, my head spins and the chief medical dwarf post is still vacant.
I have blisters where I did not know I had places.
I feel dizzy. The Overseer says it is just the mist ring. The Overseer is not a doctor.
Fever dreams again. Thrones, armor stands, then a throne wearing an armor stand.
I am sick and thirsty. The drink is right there. I cannot reach it. I know the stories.
The beast's breath made me numb. Could not even feel my disappointment. Still disappointed.
My nose went strange after the cavern trip. It smells colors now. Mostly gray.
Our healer was drafted. Into hauling.
I went to the hospital. It was a stockpile. They handed me a rock and told me to rest.
My skin is peeling and the only advice I got was 'drink more'. I would love to.
Coughing since the Safety burrow. I was one of the lucky ones. Still coughing.

good.text: I got noticeably better at my craft today. Making a thousand of anything will do that.
Smoothed so many walls I can now smooth a wall by glaring at it. Nearly.
My teacher was a dwarf from {past_fort}. He taught me to work fast and drink first.
I am the best {prof} in {fort}. I am also the only one. Both statements stand.
Learned a new trick at the anvil. The anvil was not impressed. I was.
I practised all season. Now I can do my job and hum at the same time.
Leveled up! I celebrated with a drink, which I fetched before getting thirsty. Growth.
Spent a month cutting gems. I am excellent now. Sorry, future moods.
My hands finally know what they are doing. My feet are still working on it.
Got so good at hauling I carried two things at once. Do not tell the Overseer.
I watched a master {prof} at work and absorbed it all. Mostly the swearing.
My work is now 'well-crafted'. I put it on my door so people know.
I finally understand the mist ring pumps. They pump. Water comes out. Mastery.
Got a little better at fighting. The captain nodded at me. Off duty, but he nodded.

bad.text: I trained for years as a miner. The Overseer made me a hauler. My pick has dust on it.
I joined the squad to train. The squad is 'Off duty'. My sword is now a coat hook.
Spent a whole season smoothing. My actual skill has forgotten my name.
A child out-crafted me during her mood. Plant cloth, and better than mine.
I was getting good, then the gods blinked and the Great Rewind took my progress.
I am a legendary {prof}. Today I hauled rocks. Eight hundred of them.
I asked to learn medicine. They said there are no doctors to learn from. Fair.
My skill is rusting. I can hear it. It sounds like an armor stand creaking.
Practised all day and made the same armor stand two hundred times. I learned resentment.
I was the best fisherdwarf in the fort. Then my mood wanted rough gems. You know the rest.
They put me on the wrong labor again. I am a mason doing plants in the rain.
The Overseer gave my job to a dwarf with no skill. Then charged me with a violation.
I tried to learn engraving. My first piece was a tree. It frightened people.
Nobody teaches anything here. The library is a bin and the bin knows nothing.

good.text: The air in the hall was clean today. I breathed in three times to make up for last week.
Somebody threw the refuse into the pit and it stayed there. Air and dignity restored.
The mist ring sprays right through the stink. Smells of wet rock, which I love.
The garbage pit is downwind today. I praised the wind out loud.
Walked past the catacombs and smelled nothing. They are well run, give them that.
I have smelled so much rot that I no longer notice. A gift, really.
The butcher cleaned up. I could smell the tavern again. It smells of ale and arguing.
No rotting things in the hallway this morning. I checked every corner. Twice.
The windmills are blowing the bad air somewhere else. I do not ask where.
Fresh air after a week in the depths. I nearly kissed the surface. Not the trees.
The fish cleaner has a proper room now, far from mine. Life is sweet and odorless.
I held my breath past the refuse stockpile and made it. New personal best.
The dead have been buried properly. The catacombs smell like nothing. Peace.
Clean air in {fort} today. Somebody print that in big letters.

bad.text: They hauled garbage out of the pit so it could be thrown back in. The smell did a lap.
The refuse stockpile is next to the dining hall. Somebody planned that. I want a word.
Miasma in the hallway again. The Overseer has queued smoothing to fix it. Somehow.
Rotting fish by the still. The ale tastes like the river now.
Something died in the Safety burrow and the smell came up thirty levels. Fitting.
The whole hall smells like {past_fort} near the end. You know the end I mean.
My beard has absorbed the garbage pit. I will be smelling it till spring.
Somebody left a goblin corpse on the stairs. It has been 'in a hauling queue' since summer.
The butcher worked in the hallway because the shop was full of armor stands.
I smelled rot in the temple. It was offerings, apparently. Fish offerings.
Pit stink again. The wind is coming from the dump, and the dump is coming with it.
There is miasma at the food stockpile. Dinner was eaten very quickly and quietly.
I breathed some bad air near the refuse and now everything tastes of old boots.
The stink in {fort} is so strong today, the elves at the depot left early. Silver lining.

good.text: Nobody died this week. The coffin maker is making barrels. Good sign all round.
My friend got a proper burial in the catacombs. Engraved slab, nice spot, quiet company.
The beast came up the stairs and I was not on the stairs. Simple, really.
I climbed down out of a tree before it could happen. I read the papers.
I was in the Safety burrow when the forgotten beast came. I left early. Best decision ever.
I survived the garbage pit hauling run. Eight did not. I lit a candle for each.
The memorial slab came out lovely. Even the deceased would have approved, briefly.
Felt thirsty, walked to the barrel, drank. Lived. In this world that is a story.
Grandfather died peacefully of old age. The first natural death in three forts. We cheered.
We buried the fallen and the mayor did not file a single production violation.
My mood demanded rough gems and I found one, hidden in a sock. I am alive to tell it.
The captain avenged a friend of mine. Militia of one, but a very good one.
I got a coffin of my own, ready for later. Pre-planning. Very calming.
The ghosts have been put to rest. The halls are quiet. I slept a full night.

bad.text: My friend died of thirst beside 1,994 drinks. I still cannot talk about the numbers.
A miner I knew died of thirst stuck on a tree branch. Never trust a tree.
Fifteen of us went to the Safety burrow. The beast came up the stairs. Safety, they called it.
Eight dwarves died hauling refuse out of the pit while more was thrown in. Nobody stopped.
My cousin's mood demanded rough gems. Every gem was cut. She did not finish.
A carpenter died of thirst next to 150 rough gems. Gems were not the problem.
We needed a coffin. The carpenter's queue had forty thrones ahead of it.
Lost a friend in Quakefocus waiting for the loom room. It was 'nearly ready'.
I saw a body today. Then an order came in for armor stands. Nobody even paused.
The memorial slab misspelled her name. The engraver was on smoothing duty and rushed.
My mentor died, and his job was reassigned before he was cold. To me. Thanks.
A fey miner died of thirst while the clerks counted seven silk scraps. I cannot forgive maths.
Somebody died near the execution tower and nobody is sure it was an execution.
Another funeral. The tavern ran out of drink for the wake. Somehow. Again.

good.text: It rained all day and I was underground for all of it. Perfect planning, for once.
The rain filled the cistern. Water for the mist ring, and no dwarf had to carry it.
Rain on the windmill roof sounds lovely from inside, near the ale.
I liked the rain today. It washed the garbage pit smell somewhere else.
Nobody was sent out to gather plants in the rain. Somebody upstairs is learning.
Rain this {season}, and I stayed dry. I even had a drink while watching it.
Got caught in a light drizzle. Felt like the mist ring, but free.
Stood in the doorway and watched the rain fall on the trees. Good. Stay out there, trees.
The rain chased the elves from the depot early. Kindest weather we have had.
A dwarf learns to love rain when the alternative is gathering plants in it.
Rain fell, and I was not on a tree branch. Low bar, cleared.
The storm came and I was in the tavern. The thunder sounded like approval.
A warm rain. I let it hit my face for a moment. Then I went in. Balance.
Rain on the surface means fewer goblins on the surface. That is my weather report.

bad.text: I was sent to gather plants across the whole map in the rain. The map is very big.
Soaked to the bone at the far map edge, carrying one strawberry. One.
Got rained on, then walked through the mist ring to dry off. Mistakes were made.
Rained on in the {season}. My beard has its own weather now.
I sheltered under a tree from the rain. Then I remembered the stories and ran.
The rain came in while I was hauling to the depot. Elves laughed. The rain laughed.
Wet clothes, wet socks, wet everything. Except the barrels. Still dry. Still empty.
It rained on the funeral. Even the weather ignores our safety procedures.
I hate rain. It is just water falling, and I have opinions about water.
Rain all week. The Overseer kept the plant run going anyway. Strategy, it says.
Drenched digging out the surface windmill base. The windmill stayed dry. Lucky windmill.
Rain soaked the cloth on the drying rack. The child's mood will have to wait.
Got so wet my helmet filled up. Drank some. It was not ale. Disappointing.
I got rained on, and then I got charged with tracking mud. The mayor misses nothing.

good.text: Went up to the windmill roof and saw the sky. It stayed up there. Very professional.
The sky was big today but I was bigger. Emotionally.
Stood on the walled roof and looked out over the hills. Not a goblin in sight. Lovely.
I saw a cloud shaped like a mug. Took it as a sign. Had a drink.
The sun came out. I came out. We both went back in. A good partnership.
From the execution tower you can see the whole valley. Lovely view, odd building.
Looked at the stars and counted three hundred. Then I lost count at a throne-shaped one.
The sky over {fort} is very blue. I will allow it.
I went outside and came back without being rained on or treed. Perfect day.
Watched the sunset from the parapet. Windmills turning, mist drifting. Almost elvish. Almost.
The open sky does not scare me anymore. Trees, yes. Sky, no.
Clear sky means no rain plant run. I love a clear sky for selfish reasons.
Saw a hawk. It saw me. We agreed to leave each other alone.
The moon came up over the hills like a big cut gem. Somebody tell the jeweler.

bad.text: They sent me outside and there was sky all over the place. No ceiling at all.
The sky is too big. Somewhere under it are goblins. Several armies' worth.
I went up the windmill stairs and the sky was just there. Waiting. I came down.
The sun looked at me. I looked back. I lost.
Out on the surface I could see a dark fortress on the horizon. I would rather not.
Got dizzy on the roof. Sky above, nothing in between. Who builds like this?
A bird landed on my helmet. It acted like it owned the place. The sky breeds arrogance.
I looked up and stepped into the mist ring. Lesson learned: never look up.
The plant run took me so far out I lost sight of the fort. Only sky and trees. Terrifying.
There was nothing between me and the sky except a tree, and I do not trust trees.
The sky turned dark at noon. The Overseer said keep gathering. The sky agreed with me.
I miss having a roof. I am under a roof. I miss it anyway, from the trip.
Too much sky this {season}. Somebody should build a ceiling over it.
I saw a cloud shaped like an armor stand. Even the weather has a work order.

good.text: Got thirsty, walked to the barrel and drank. I did not die beside it. Very modern of me.
There are thousands of drinks in the stockpile and I personally had one of them.
The carpenter made barrels instead of doors this week. The ale is flowing. I am flowing.
I got a drink before the thirst got me. Remember the miner and his 1,994 drinks.
The tavern keeper poured me a mug without being asked. I may marry the tavern.
Fresh brew from the second still. Two stills! We are an empire.
Drank so well this week I forgot the Quakefocus famine for an hour.
My mug was full, my bench was free and nobody mentioned smoothing. Paradise.
Had a drink with the captain. The militia's whole membership, toasting itself.
Ale in the morning, ale at noon. The Overseer queued brewing and nobody cancelled it.
The drink stockpile is next to my workshop now. Whoever planned that, I salute you.
Tasted a dwarven wine so good I briefly wished the liaison would ask for it at 210 percent.
I drank by the mist ring. Wet on the outside, happy on the inside.
I have never been thirsty in {fort}. Do not jinx it by printing this.

bad.text: I died of thirst twice in my dreams last night, each time beside a full barrel.
The drinks are all 'in use'. Nobody can tell me what they are being used for.
There is ale. There is a mug. There is me. And yet somehow I am thirsty.
No barrels, so no brewing. The carpenter is on doors. The doors are not thirsty.
The brewer has been hauling stone all week. Eight hundred stones. Zero ale.
Drank water from the cistern. Tasted of windmill. I am ashamed.
The drink stockpile is behind forty bins of armor stand parts. I can see it. I cannot reach it.
Nearly went the way of the miner on the branch. Climbing down came before ale, barely.
I asked for a drink and was handed a work order. They are not the same.
We have 2,000 drinks and one tavern keeper, and the tavern keeper is on smoothing.
Sober for three days. My beard has started making decisions without me.
Somebody brewed everything into one flavor. It is the flavor of desperation.
Ran out of ale during the {season}. Ran into the mist ring for comfort. Not the same.
They counted the drinks and said there were plenty. They did not say where.

good.text: Meat! Actual meat! Searabbeys waited years for this. I ate it slowly, for them.
I had a real roast today. It tasted like the end of the Meat Watch.
Ate a lavish meal and nobody asked me to make a throne after. Simple joys.
The fishers caught something and the cook cooked it. Teamwork, at last.
A perfect plump helmet. Crisp, earthy, not on fire. Ten out of ten.
Food in the stockpile, food in the kitchen, food on my plate. {past_fort} could never.
I had second helpings. Nobody said 'famine, day 32'. Bliss.
Tried a stew with goblin-free vegetables. Delicious and patriotic.
The cook made a masterwork meal. I ate the masterwork. No regrets.
Ate dinner without worrying that it was the last one. Personal growth.
Somebody smoked fish beside the windmills. Smells like wind and victory.
The kitchen was busy all day. I heard sizzling. Best sound in {fort}.
Biscuits with a mug of ale. Nobody died. That is a full menu.
There were seventeen plants for ten dwarves once. Today I ate seventeen plants alone.

bad.text: Plump helmets again. Raw. Unwashed. Glaring at me.
Day 32 of the famine, said the old Quakefocus paper. Some days I still count.
No meat for ages. The ghost of the Meat Watch has taken a seat at my table.
Seventeen plants for ten dwarves. I remember it. My stomach remembers it louder.
The fisherdwarf had a strange mood and wanted rough gems. No fish. No gems. No luck.
My meal was left beside the garbage pit. Then it was hauled back out. Then in.
The cook is on smoothing duty. Dinner is a raw turnip and a smoothed wall.
The food stockpile is buried behind thrones. I can smell dinner, but cannot reach it.
I ate something that might have been a cave spider. I am not asking.
All the meals went to the depot. The liaison said there is much to share. With him.
I ate the same quarry bush leaves for a month. My beard has gone slightly green.
The Overseer sent the hunters to gather plants. In the rain. Again.
My dinner was confiscated as evidence in a production order violation.
Ate cold food in the hall because the kitchen was full of armor stands.

good.text: Ate in the dining hall at a real table. Nobody stored an armor stand on it.
The dining room has been smoothed and engraved. My soup tasted twice as good.
I ate on a throne. One of the hundred in stock found its way to the hall. Quite comfy.
Sat by the window over the mist ring. Watched the spray while eating. Fine dining.
The tavern and the dining hall are next door. Whoever planned this deserves a medal.
Shared a table with the captain. He told stories of being off duty. Many stories.
Got the good chair, the one that does not wobble. A rare honor.
A whole dinner without a single dwarf mentioning thirst. We dined like nobles.
The dining hall is so fine now, the elves at the depot asked for a tour. We said no.
I ate dinner in a room with walls, a floor and a ceiling. Luxury, by {past_fort} standards.
Long tables, hot food, loud dwarves. That is the {fort} I signed up for.
Clean table, clean mug, clean conscience. Dinner was a triumph.
The engraving above my seat shows a feast. Art imitating my plate. Lovely.
Sat next to a stranger who loved the windmills too. Best dinner of the year.

bad.text: Ate standing up again. The chairs were all assigned to the throne stockpile.
There were armor stands at every table. I ate with my elbows touching steel.
The dining hall is full of bins of loose stones. I ate on a bin. It was rude to me.
A hundred and forty dwarves and one dining hall. My elbow is in someone's stew.
The dining room is on the smoothing list. We dine among rough stone, like animals.
My table wobbles. I have reported it. The report went to the mayor and was filed as a crime.
The dining hall shares a wall with the garbage pit. Atmosphere: notable.
I ate on the floor. The floor was rough. The meal was rougher.
Sat in the only empty chair. Turned out it was the ghost's chair. It made that clear.
No tables at all this week. Somebody used the wood for thrones.
The dining hall is thirty levels away from the kitchen. My meal arrived cold and tired.
Somebody built the dining room under the execution tower. Dinner conversation is grim.
No room in the hall, so I ate on the stairs. The stairs to 'Safety'. Lost my appetite.
The mist ring blows into the dining hall. Wet bread is not a dish.

good.text: Slept a full night in my own bed. No armor stands moved in while I was out.
I dreamed of full barrels, and when I woke up, they were still full.
A whole night's sleep and no sudden call to the Safety burrow. Glorious.
Woke up rested for the first time since {past_fort}. Felt like a new dwarf. Slightly confused.
The windmills hum all night. Best lullaby in the fort.
I napped in the mist ring garden. Woke up damp and serene.
I slept so well I missed the morning work order. The orders survived without me.
I dreamed I was the mayor and filed no violations. A sweet, impossible dream.
My bed is soft, my door is shut and the beasts are far below. Sleep came easily.
Slept through a goblin rumor. Woke up and it was still a rumor. Perfect.
I took a nap on a throne in the stockpile. The Overseer did not notice. Bliss.
Woke up in my own bed instead of on a tree branch. Small victories.
A quiet night. Even the ghost was off duty, like the militia.
Slept in on a rainy morning while the others went plant-gathering. Sorry. Not sorry.

bad.text: Slept on the floor again. All the beds are 'reserved' by the Overseer.
Woken up at dawn by the sound of somebody smoothing my wall. Smoothing is loud.
I dreamed of armor stands. Thousands. All saluting me. I woke up screaming.
Dozed off by the garbage pit and woke up being hauled to the pit. Narrow escape.
My bed has been replaced with a throne. You cannot sleep on a throne. I tried.
Fell asleep in the hall and woke up in the Safety burrow. I do not know how. I ran.
The mist ring blew in through the door all night. I slept in a cloud.
Could not sleep. Kept thinking of the miner with 1,994 drinks. I got up and drank.
I was so tired I slept in the hallway. Three dwarves hauled stones over me.
I had a nightmare that the gods blinked and I lost a whole season. Then it happened.
Up all night listening for the forgotten beast on the stairs. It never came. This time.
Too many snoring dwarves in the dormitory. A hundred and forty, all in tune.
Slept badly. The engraving on my ceiling is of a famine. It watches me.
I dozed off on duty and the mayor charged me with an order violation. In my sleep.

heads_good.text: WOKE UP NOT IN A TREE

good.text: I prayed to {deity} for no more thrones. The order ended. I am now very devout.
The temple was a temple today, not a stockpile. {deity} and I had the place to ourselves.
Prayed to {deity} for a drink and someone handed me one. Faith confirmed.
I lit a candle for the fallen of the Safety burrow. {deity} listened. I am sure.
Knelt by the altar and felt peace. Then the windmills creaked. Peace with sound effects.
I asked {deity} to watch over the trees. Not the trees, the dwarves near them.
Prayed for the miners of {past_fort}. Felt lighter, like a dwarf without a work order.
{deity} sent a sign: a full barrel nobody had claimed. I claimed it, devoutly.
Spent a calm hour at the shrine. Nobody hauled bins through it. A holy day.
I thanked {deity} for the mist ring. It may have been a mechanic's work, but I hedged.
My prayers got better since the temple got smoothed. Acoustics matter.
Prayed before the goblins came. They did not come. {deity} is clearly on the job.
I asked {deity} for one rough gem for the next mood. I found one in a sock. A miracle.
Long prayer, short sermon, good ale after. That is religion in {fort}.

bad.text: I went to pray and the temple was full of armor stands. {deity} is behind them somewhere.
Prayed for an end to smoothing. Got two more smoothing jobs. {deity} has a sense of humor.
I prayed to {deity} for a doctor. The chief medical dwarf post is still vacant.
No priest, no altar, no candle. I prayed into a bin. The bin did not answer.
The shrine is next to the garbage pit. Prayers rise. So does the smell.
Prayed for rough gems for my friend's mood. Every gem had been cut that morning.
I knelt to pray and knelt on a rock. One of the hundreds. {deity} must have placed it.
I prayed to {deity} during the Safety burrow evacuation. I am alive. Many are not. Mixed.
I have not been to temple in months. The Overseer keeps scheduling smoothing over it.
Prayed for drink beside a full barrel. Realised what I was doing. Drank. Felt foolish.
The altar is rough stone and on the smoothing list. Even the gods must wait.
I prayed for rain to stop. It did. Then I was sent to gather plants anyway.
{deity} has been quiet since the Great Rewind. Perhaps they lost a season too.
My prayer was interrupted by a hauler carrying refuse out of the pit. Through the temple.

good.text: Had a lovely chat about the old forts. We agreed Quakefocus had the best thrones. All of them.
Heard a rumor the Overseer cancelled the armor stand order. Even if false, it was nice to hear.
Talked with a dwarf from {past_fort}. She told me how it {past_fort_fate}. We laughed. Then sighed.
Somebody told me a joke about the Safety burrow. Too soon, but I laughed anyway.
I argued about whether trees are evil and I won. They are.
Long talk with the captain about the militia. He has big plans for the nine empty places.
The liaison spoke for an hour and I understood one sentence. There is much to share.
Heard news that our kin reclaimed an old fort from the goblins. Good for them.
A {prof} told me their whole life story. It was mostly hauling. Strangely moving.
We talked about the goblin armies until the ale ran low. Good times, bad goblins.
Swapped tips on how not to die of thirst. Tip one: drink. Very well received.
Had a long talk in the mist ring. Both of us got soaked. Worth it.
Gossiped about who will become mayor next. Everyone said 'not me'. A lovely chorus.
Caught up with an old friend. We did not mention the garbage pit once. Mature of us.

bad.text: The liaison cornered me. 'There is much to share', he said. For three hours.
Someone talked about thrones all through dinner. I have made hundreds. I do not want to talk.
Got a lecture on smoothing technique from a dwarf with a sixteen-thousand-job queue.
Argued with a ghost from {past_fort}. It wanted the loom room. I had no answers.
Overheard dwarves planning a trip to the Safety burrow. I said nothing. I should have.
The mayor talked to me for an hour about production order violations. Mine, mostly.
An elf at the depot talked about trees. The trees here kill people. I said so. Awkward.
Heard gossip in the tavern. It was about me. It was accurate. That is worse.
Somebody told me the Torments of Hating still live in Searabbeys. I did not need that.
Tried to chat with the captain. He was off duty from conversations too.
A dwarf would not stop talking about rough gems. Her mood is coming. I could tell.
Talked about the thirst paradox at lunch and suddenly everyone got thirsty.
A goblin rumor ruined my afternoon. {enemy} is busy, apparently.
I tried to talk about my feelings. Somebody handed me a work order instead.

good.text: Saw an engraving of a dwarf drinking beside a barrel. Finally, art with a happy ending.
The new statue is of a dwarf, not a throne. After all those thrones, that felt bold.
Admired the mace Claspedserpent in my dreams. Fine silver. Quakefocus got one thing right.
A masterwork engraving of the windmills went up in the hall. I stared at it for an hour.
The mural in the tavern shows the founding of {fort}. Nobody is thirsty in it. Lovely.
I saw a figurine of the militia captain. Off duty, of course. Very lifelike.
The engraving of the mist ring is so good I got wet looking at it.
Someone carved a perfect little mug. I tried to drink from it. No regrets.
There is an engraving of the 1,981 armor stands. It is huge. And somehow moving.
Our engraver made a picture of a happy goblin-free sky. Fantasy, but nice fantasy.
I saw a portrait of the liaison. It even looks like it has much to share.
A child made a cloth doll during her mood. The plant cloth was worth it.
The statue garden has a statue of a dwarf drinking water. Bold. Moving. Confusing.
Saw the art of a {prof}. Better than mine. I will not mention this to anyone.

bad.text: The engraving in the hall shows the Quakefocus famine. Seventeen plants. Very detailed.
The only art in the fort is armor stands. I have stopped calling it art.
Someone engraved a tree on my wall. It has a miner in it. I asked for a refund.
The sculptor was sent to smoothing. My statue is now a half-done lump called 'Untitled'.
A dwarf in a mood demanded rough gems. All gems were cut. No artifact. Only silence.
My finest figurine was sold to the elves. They said there is much to share. They took it.
There is an engraving of the Safety burrow. It shows fifteen dwarves. Too soon.
The new statue blocks the path to the still. Beautiful art. Thirsty art.
Somebody engraved the garbage pit. The pit is now in two places. Too many pits.
I wanted to make art, but the Overseer wanted another throne. The throne won.
Our finest artifact is still in {past_fort}, which {past_fort_fate}. Art, held hostage.
The engraving of the forgotten beast is too accurate. People take the long way now.
Saw an ugly mug. I made it. I am my own harshest critic, and also correct.
A masterwork bracelet went into a bin with loose stones. Art, buried alive.

good.text: The captain fought off a goblin all by himself. A militia of one, and that one is enough.
I hit a goblin with a mug. The mug survived. So did I. The goblin less so.
Sparred with the captain and kept all my teeth. He says I have promise. Also, he is lonely.
We used one of the armor stands for actual armor. A historic day for the stockpile.
The forgotten beast was killed before it found the stairs. Safest the burrow has ever been.
I joined the squad. The squad is now two. Our enemies should be worried. Slightly.
Dodged a spear, then went for a drink. Combat is mostly knowing when to leave.
The siege ended and nobody I know got hurt. I cheered from the tavern.
Trained all morning. I now know which end of the axe is the friendly end.
Watched the captain fight from the parapet. Windmills turning behind him. Like a painting.
A goblin scout ran off when he saw us. Probably the mist ring. It is very intimidating.
I won a wrestling match against a kobold thief. He took nothing. I took his dignity.
Took the war of {civ} against {enemy} very personally today and hit a practice dummy hard.
The {enemy_race}s of {enemy} came, saw the walls, and went home. Walls are underrated.

bad.text: The goblins attacked and the squad was 'Off duty'. The squad is always off duty.
Our militia is one captain and nine empty spots. I counted the spots. They did not fight.
We have two thousand armor stands and no armor. Somebody explain the plan.
I fought a goblin with a mug because the weapons were all in a bin at the far map edge.
Was drafted in the middle of my sandwich. The sandwich did not survive the war.
The forgotten beast came up the stairs. The stairs were the plan. That was the whole plan.
Ambushed while gathering plants among the trees. The trees helped the ambush. I know it.
Sparred with a training partner who turned out to be a door. I lost.
The captain stood alone at the gate. I watched from behind him. Very far behind him.
Told to hide in the Safety burrow during the siege. I hid in the tavern. I am alive.
The {enemy_race}s of {enemy} burned our surface windmill. The mist ring has stopped. War is cruel.
{enemy} is at war with {civ} and nobody told the militia. Or the militia knew and napped.
I lost a fight to a turkey. It was a large turkey. Please do not print the size.
I trained for a whole season and then the Overseer made me a hauler. My axe hauls now.

heads_bad.text: FOUGHT A GOBLIN WITH A MUG

good.text: The thirsty ghost finally got a memorial slab. It went quiet. I think it found a drink.
A ghost walked past me and said nothing. Polite ghost. Better than some neighbours.
We engraved a slab for the miner who died in the tree. He has stopped knocking on branches.
The ghost in the dining hall waved at me. I waved back. We are on waving terms.
No haunting this week. Even the ghosts seem to have gone off duty.
The ghost helped me find a barrel. It knows where all the barrels are. It learned too late.
A ghost from {past_fort} came by and said it is proud of us. Then it rattled a chain.
The ghost of a hauler kept hauling. Honestly, he got more done than the living.
I put a mug on the grave. In the morning it was empty. I am choosing to be happy about this.
A ghost told me the Safety burrow is a trap. Most useful ghost so far.
The catacombs are calm. The dead are at rest. The slabs are lovely. Good management.
Saw a ghost with a full beard and a fine helmet. Very stylish. Afterlife goals.
The ghost said to tell everyone: drink BEFORE you get thirsty. I am passing it on.
Our new memorial hall has room for everyone. Grim, but well planned. I approve.

bad.text: A ghost stood by the barrel all night asking why it died of thirst. Nobody had an answer.
The ghost of a hauler keeps throwing refuse back into the pit. Or out of it. Hard to say.
A ghost asked me for a rough gem. All the gems are cut. Even the dead are stuck in moods.
There is a ghost in the Safety burrow. It wants to warn us. Nobody goes down there to listen.
The ghost of the tree miner is still in the tree. The tree seems smug about it.
A ghost knocked over a stack of armor stands. There were a thousand. It took all night.
The ghost of the old mayor still files violation charges. They still go through.
Saw a ghost from {past_fort}. It said the place {past_fort_fate}. Then it looked at me. Long look.
A ghost woke me to complain about the smoothing. Even the dead are in the queue.
Our dead have no slabs because the mason is on throne duty. They have noticed.
The ghost in the tavern drinks nothing and stares at the mugs. It spoils the mood.
A ghost followed me to the well. Then to the barrel. It does not trust me with water.
The ghost of a weaver keeps asking if the loom room is ready. It is not.
I was haunted all week by somebody I never met. Very rude of them.

heads_good.text: SPOOKED, BUT IN A FUN WAY

good.text: A cat sat on my lap all evening. I did not move. I would not have moved for a siege.
Our dog brought me a mug. Empty, but it is the thought that counts.
The herd is in the big indoor pasture now. Nobody is wandering into trees. Including me.
I petted a yak today. It looked at me like I was worth something.
A goat ignored me. Not rudely. Kindly. As if to say: 'You have enough going on'.
The new pasture has walls. The animals stay put. I wish the plant gatherers did.
Our fisherdwarf caught three fish and no mood. A lucky day for everyone.
A bird landed on the windmill and just sat there. Nice view. Smart bird.
The dogs met the elves at the depot and barked. Good dogs. Very good dogs.
A kitten followed me to work. I worked twice as slowly and three times as happily.
The war dog wears a little helmet now. He is the second-best soldier we have.
Watched the sheep get sheared. Wool for the cloth shortage! The child's mood is saved.
There are so many dogs here we could make a second militia. A better one.
I named the new calf after the captain. Both are brave and mostly stand around.

bad.text: A dog ate my meal. Then my second meal. Then looked at me as if I owed him a third.
Found a cat asleep in the ale barrel. I drank from another one. Mostly.
A llama spat at me while I was being virtuous. Unprovoked.
A goat got into the tavern and drank better than I did this week.
The herd wandered into the trees and we had to fetch them. Through the trees. In the rain.
We have more dogs than beds. Some of the beds are dogs now.
Ducks ate the plump helmet crop. The ducks look very pleased. We have seventeen plants left.
A carp bit the fisher. The fisher bit back. Neither will talk about it.
The cats have claimed the dining hall. I eat in the hallway now, under orders from a cat.
The animals are kept by the garbage pit. The animals have complained. So have I.
Somebody tamed a cave crocodile and put it next to the well. Nobody gets water now.
The mules carried my bin to the depot and I had to carry the mules back. Long story.
An elf at the depot told me my pig looks sad. My pig was fine until the elf.
A turkey chased me across the pasture. I have told nobody. Do not print this.

good.text: The caravan brought empty barrels. Empty barrels! The brewer cried. I cried.
I sold an armor stand to a trader. One down. Several thousand to go.
The liaison said something other than 'There is much to share'. I missed what it was.
Got a bargain at the depot: two cloth bolts for one throne. We have plenty of thrones.
The merchants loved our mugs. Our mugs are very good. I make our mugs.
The depot was clear of junk today. The wagon got in. Trade happened. Wonderful.
We sold a stack of thrones at a profit. The Overseer was right all along, maybe.
The elves finally left. Trade went fine. Mostly the leaving part.
The caravan brought meat. Real meat. I bought some and hugged the yak driver.
Traded smoothed stone blocks for ale. We trade stone for ale. Perfect economy.
A merchant asked for a cut gem and I said no. Some mood will need it. I am learning.
The broker called my work 'remarkable'. He then bought it for very little. Still remarkable.
News from the caravan: {civ} is doing well. Good. Somebody should be.
The liaison from {civ} came, sat, drank and left. Smoothest visit yet.

bad.text: The liaison wants rings. Lots of rings. At a big markup. We have armor stands.
We sold the last rough gem to the merchants. A mood started the next morning. Of course.
The caravan came with no meat and no barrels. Just cloth and opinions.
An elf refused my wooden mug because a tree died for it. Several of ours died because of trees.
The wagon could not reach the depot. The road is lined with thrones.
We traded away our barrels for beads. Now we are thirsty and glittering.
I was paid in armor stands. I already have armor stands. Everyone does.
The merchant was charged with a production order violation by the mayor. Trade ended early.
{liaison} came and said there is much to share. Then asked what we could give.
The trader had heard about the thirst paradox. He sold us water at a premium.
We offered the merchants thrones. They said they heard we had a lot. They were laughing.
Spent all day hauling goods to the depot. Spent all evening hauling them back.
The caravan brought news that {enemy} is on the march. I would have preferred cheese.
Nobody told me the caravan came. I missed the only cheese seller of the year.

good.text: {about} has me feeling {adj}. Write it down before the Overseer queues something.
I am {adj} about {about}. In this fort, you grab a good feeling and hold it tight.
Honestly? {about} left me {adj}. Better than the last fort, I will say that.
If you had told me {about} would make me {adj}, I would have laughed. And I did, today.
Life is good. Nobody is thirsty, no trees are near me and the windmills are turning.
I am feeling fine. Not great, not thirsty, fine. That is high praise here.
Today went well. I suspect a mistake somewhere, but I will not look for it.
I woke up, I worked, I drank, I ate. Nothing fell on me. Excellent.
Whatever it was, it was good. I do not need details. I need a mug to celebrate.
I am happy. The Overseer does not know yet. Do not tell it, it may queue something.
I have decided this is a good day, and I will hear no arguments.
I am feeling {adj}, and {about} is to blame. Thank you, {about}.
Things in {fort} are going well. Do not print that too loudly.
We are doing better than {past_fort}, which {past_fort_fate}. Low bar, cleared nicely.

bad.text: {about}. Just thinking about it makes me {adj}. Put that in the paper.
I am {adj} about {about}, and also about everything else, to be fair.
{about} left me {adj}. Last time I felt like this, we were making thrones.
It is complicated. It involves {about}. I am {adj}. Do not ask follow-ups.
I blame the Overseer. I do not know for what. The Overseer will know.
I sat in the mist ring and sulked. Wet sulking is still sulking.
I feel like a throne in a stockpile. Built for greatness. Stored forever.
This is {fort}. Things happen. Usually to me.
It has been one of those days. You know. Thirst, trees, orders, rain.
All the gems are cut, all the barrels are full, and I am still unhappy. Explain that.
I am sad and I do not know why. My guess is the armor stands. It is usually the armor stands.
I would complain to the mayor, but the mayor's office is vacant. So is my patience.
I hoped {fort} would be better than {past_fort}. That one {past_fort_fate}. We are trying.
I keep thinking about the {record} at {record_fort}. We must not repeat it. We will.
